prompt: Match each thing that varies to how it appears in fleet.

pairs.right: A file per application and environment

prompt: When does a repository layout fail, by the lesson's measure?

choices.text: When the application and cluster repositories are separate
choices.why: That is the layout the lesson recommends.

choices.text: When two environments share an image tag
choices.why: Sharing a release is the goal of promotion.

choices.text: When it has more than two top-level directories
choices.why: The number of directories is not the measure.

choices.text: When one kind of change needs edits in several places
choices.why: Right. One of them is eventually forgotten, and environments drift.

prompt: Which of the three changes most often?

choices.text: The application
choices.why: Right. Many commits a day, by the developers.

choices.text: The configuration, since every pod restart rewrites it
choices.why: A restart changes nothing in Git.

choices.text: They all change at the same pace
choices.why: The point of the section is that they do not.

choices.text: The environment, because every release creates one for testing
choices.why: Environments come and go rarely in this lesson's model.

prompt: Where do the application's repository and fleet meet?

choices.text: At the image
choices.why: Right. CI builds and pushes it; a pull request to fleet references it.

choices.text: At Gitea's branch protection, shared between them
choices.why: Protection is per repository, and bulletin has none.

choices.text: At the Kustomization, which reads both repositories
choices.why: Flux reads fleet only.

choices.text: At a shared main branch that both repositories merge into
choices.why: They are separate repositories with separate histories.

prompt: Which reasons does the lesson give for two repositories? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: They have different owners
choices.why: Right. Production's rule should not slow down code.

choices.text: They change at different speeds
choices.why: Right. Promotions would be buried among code commits.

choices.text: Flux refuses repositories that contain a Dockerfile
choices.why: Flux reads paths and ignores what it does not need.

choices.text: Git cannot hold YAML and code in one repository
choices.why: It can; a monorepo is a legitimate choice.

prompt: The commit the image bulletin:1.0 was built from carries the Git ___ v1.0 in the bulletin repository.
Why does promoting by merging a staging branch into a production branch go wrong?

choices.text: A merge brings every staging commit
choices.why: Right. Including the staging-only ones, which then need cherry-picks to keep out.

choices.text: Git refuses merges between long-lived branches
choices.why: It merges them; the trouble is what comes along.

choices.text: Flux cannot follow a branch other than main
choices.why: A Kustomization's source can follow any branch.

choices.text: Branches cannot hold different replica counts
choices.why: They can, which is part of the drift.

prompt: With one directory per environment, what does a promotion's diff contain?

choices.text: The whole production directory, rewritten
choices.why: Only the changed lines appear.

choices.text: Only the release being promoted
choices.why: Right. Production's directory changes to say what staging's says about it, and nothing else.

choices.text: Every commit made to staging since the last promotion
choices.why: That is what a branch merge carries.

choices.text: Nothing, because Flux copies staging to production
choices.why: Nothing copies between directories; a person changes production.

prompt: staging moved to apps/bulletin/staging in one pull request. Why were no pods recreated?

choices.text: The pods were protected by a PodDisruptionBudget
choices.why: No budget exists here, and none was needed.

choices.text: Flux ignores moves inside a repository
choices.why: It noticed: the revision changed and it applied from the new path.

choices.text: git mv keeps the file's hash, so Flux skipped it
choices.why: Flux compares objects with the cluster, not file hashes.

choices.text: The same Kustomization still owned them
choices.why: Right. Same objects, same owner, a different directory.

prompt: A move takes manifests into a directory that a different Kustomization reads. What happens to a PersistentVolumeClaim among them?

choices.text: Nothing, because claims are never pruned
choices.why: Flux prunes any object it applied that left its path.

choices.text: It is transferred between Kustomizations untouched
choices.why: Ownership is not transferred; the first one prunes what left its path.

choices.text: It is deleted and recreated empty
choices.why: Right. The first Kustomization prunes it and the second creates a new one.

choices.text: The merge is refused by Gitea
choices.why: Gitea knows nothing about Kustomizations.

prompt: Why did validate.sh need changing in this lesson?

choices.text: kubeconform needed a newer Kubernetes version
choices.why: The version stayed 1.37.0.

choices.text: Gitea renamed the validate context
choices.why: The context is whatever the script posts.

choices.text: It checked $work/staging, which the move removed
choices.why: Right. Pointed at apps/, it checks every application and environment.

choices.text: The ci token had expired
choices.why: Nothing expired.

prompt: What does dependsOn: staging do for the production Kustomization?

choices.text: It reconciles production only while staging is ready
choices.why: Right. It orders; it does not promote.

choices.text: It copies staging's image to production
choices.why: Production runs what its own directory says.

choices.text: It makes production a namespace inside staging
choices.why: Namespaces do not nest.

choices.text: It deletes production when staging is deleted
choices.why: Pruning is per Kustomization, not through dependencies.

prompt: On which port of your machine does production's bulletin answer?
Order the promotion of bulletin 1.1.
items: Tag v1.1 in the bulletin repository
Build and push the image bulletin:1.1
Merge a pull request moving staging to 1.1
Merge a pull request moving production to 1.1
trap: The image exists before any environment names it, and staging runs it before production does.

prompt: After bulletin:1.1 was pushed, what did staging run before the first pull request?

choices.text: Both, one pod each
choices.why: Only the directory's image runs.
Right. A registry is not a deployment; nothing named 1.1 yet.

choices.text: Neither, while Flux checked the new image
choices.why: Flux was not watching the registry.

choices.text: 1.1, as soon as the push finished
choices.why: The push changes no cluster.

prompt: The diff of the two environments' files showed five differences. Which one was the release in transit?

choices.text: The image
choices.why: Right. Namespace, replicas, message and port are meant to differ.

choices.text: The nodePort
choices.why: Each environment has its own port on purpose.

choices.text: The namespace
choices.why: It is what makes them two environments.

choices.text: The replica count
choices.why: That difference is deliberate, per environment.

prompt: Version 1.1 of index.cgi adds a line that prints the name of the ___ that answered.
What did CODEOWNERS do when a pull request touched apps/bulletin/production/?

choices.text: Refused the merge until Bruno approved
choices.why: That needs block_on_official_review_requests in the protection.

choices.text: Requested Bruno's review
choices.why: Right. It routes reviews; it does not require them on its own.

choices.text: Moved the pull request to Bruno's fork
choices.why: Nothing moved; Bruno was added as a reviewer.

choices.text: Approved the change on Bruno's behalf
choices.why: Nothing approves for a person.

prompt: Why would ownership by directory be impossible if staging and production shared one file?

choices.text: Flux would apply the file twice
choices.why: Flux applies what a path holds, once.

choices.text: Nobody could own one without owning the other
choices.why: Right. Ownership is by path, and one path would hold both.

choices.text: Gitea limits CODEOWNERS to one entry per file
choices.why: The limit is not in Gitea; it is in the layout.

choices.text: CODEOWNERS ignores YAML files
choices.why: It matches any path.

prompt: In the many-clusters layout, what does adding a production region mean?

choices.text: A new directory under clusters/
choices.why: Right. It points at the same apps/bulletin/production/.

choices.text: A new Gitea server
choices.why: One repository describes every cluster.

choices.text: A copy of apps/bulletin/production/ per region
choices.why: The configuration is shared, not copied, until two regions need to differ.

choices.text: A new branch for the region
choices.why: Environments and clusters are directories, not branches.

prompt: Which Argo CD object generates one Application per cluster from a template?

choices.text: The root Application
choices.why: It applies Application files; it generates none.

choices.text: A Kustomization
choices.why: That is Flux's object.

choices.text: An ApplicationSet
choices.why: Right. From a list, or from the clusters Argo CD knows.

choices.text: An AppProject
choices.why: A project limits what Applications may do.

prompt: A Kustomization's path no longer exists after a move. What does Flux do to the objects it applied before?

choices.text: Moves them to the new path
choices.why: Flux does not guess where a path went.

choices.text: Recreates them from the cache
choices.why: Nothing is recreated; the Kustomization stays not ready.

choices.text: Leaves them as they are
choices.why: Right. It reports kustomization path not found and changes nothing.

choices.text: Prunes them all
choices.why: An unreadable path is not taken as an empty one.

prompt: Before merging a rename of a Kustomization in clusters/, what does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Search for the old name across the directory
choices.why: Right. A dependsOn naming the old one would wait for ever.

choices.text: Suspend every Kustomization
choices.why: Nothing needs suspending for a rename.

choices.text: Rename the namespace too
choices.why: A Kustomization's name and a namespace are unrelated.

choices.text: Delete the old Kustomization by hand first
choices.why: Pruning the old one is Flux's job once the file changes.

prompt: Production needs a fix that staging does not have yet. In this layout, what is the change?

choices.text: A pull request to production's directory
choices.why: Right. It can be made, reviewed and owned on its own, and staging catches up after.

choices.text: kubectl edit in production, then a commit
choices.why: The reconciler would undo the edit before the commit lands.

choices.text: A hotfix branch merged into main later
choices.why: Environments are directories; the branch would be main either way.

choices.text: A new environment called hotfix
choices.why: An environment is not needed for one change.
